subject: Technical deep dive: latency & throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Technical deep dive: latency & throughput SLOs

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the deep-dive earlier today. Posting a short recap so we have a shared record and next steps. Please flag anything I missed or misunderstood.

Pain points & goals discussed:
- Real-time search latency is the priority: goal is sub-200ms p50 for single-query search and p99 target of ~500–600ms (goalable).
- Throughput: current peak expected during business hours ~800–1200 QPS; sustained baseline ~300–500 QPS. Bursting behavior matters (short spikes up to ~2k QPS).
- Model requirements: ability to run a transformer-based reranker (context length ~1024 tokens); embeddings for semantic matching with 512-d vectors; support for mixed workloads (short chat-style generation + batch reranking).
- Deployment/security: customer wants VPC/private deployment with customer-managed KMS and audit logs; ability to white-list CIDRs and support for private peering.

Suggested topology & options we covered:
- Dedicated Redwood pool (reserved capacity) in us-west region for primary traffic; cross-region read replica in us-east for DR/fallback.
- Autoscaling policy: target 80% utilization on preferred instance types; burst capacity via spare pooled nodes to handle spikes.
- Model variants: quantized 8-bit variant for batching/reranking to lower cost; smaller 7B-style encoder for embeddings if throughput constrained.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated context + local LRU for hot keys to reduce p99.

Open questions / clarifications we requested:
1) Can you share sample QPS time-series (15m resolution) and representative payload sizes? (we attached sample-payloads.json)
2) Any hard p99 SLAs we should design to (e.g., legal/contractual)?
3) Network constraints: outbound/inbound port policies and VPN details — can you share the diagram?

Attachments included: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (proposal + rough sizing), sample-payloads.json.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa/Michael: deliver a sizing recommendation and POC plan by EOD Tue (2027-04-20).
- Acme: share QPS time-series and network diagram by Mon (2027-04-19).
- Schedule POC kickoff (30–60 minute technical kickoff) — propose Wed 2027-04-21 14:00 PT or Thu 2027-04-22 10:00 PT.

Thanks — happy to adjust any numbers if I misunderstood.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Technical deep dive: latency & throughput SLOs

Hi Marissa —

This looks great and captures most of it. A few clarifications/notes from our side:

- Latency targets: product team is pushing for p50 <= 150ms and p99 <= 600ms for the interactive search path. If p50 is achievable at 150ms that would be great; we realize p99 will be harder and want to understand tail mitigation strategies.
- Throughput: the 800–1200 QPS is correct as baseline peak for our west coast users. We do have occasional weekend spikes up to ~1800 QPS (not sustained longer than ~10–15 minutes).
- Payloads: typical request size is small (avg 250 tokens) but we do have batched rerank jobs (up to batch size 64) for nightly re-rank runs — those can be routed to a lower-cost quantized path.
- Security: we need SOC 2 evidence and support for our in-house KMS (AWS KMS CMKs). We also plan to require private peering; I attached our network diagram.

I attached acme-network-diagram.png and a short CSV with sample timeseries.

Two asks: can Michael or someone on your infra team confirm whether the proposed autoscale + burst pool design can support a 2k QPS 10–15 minute spike without manual intervention? Also please confirm whether suffix-based KV caching would help our tail.

Thanks —
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Director, Search Platform | Acme Corp
[Attachment: acme-network-diagram.png (image/png)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Technical deep dive: latency & throughput SLOs

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the quick replies and attachments — received the network diagram and time-series. Short answers to your asks and next actions:

- Autoscale + burst pool: Michael (cc'd) will validate sizing; initial sizing in the attached PDF assumes burst capacity via warm spare nodes and autoscale cooldowns tuned to avoid oscillation. We should be able to absorb a 2k QPS 10–15 minute spike without manual intervention provided the warm pool is sized to ~20% of your peak — Michael, I'll let you add any notes.
- Tail mitigation: suffix/KV caching plus request hedging around model variants typically brings p99 down substantially for repeated keys; we'll include concrete experiments in the POC plan.
- SOC 2 / KMS: we support customer-managed CMKs and can provide the SOC 2 report & controls mapping. I will attach the evidence and a link to our compliance packet in the POC folder.

Confirmed next steps & owners:
- Marissa/Michael: POC sizing & plan + runbook (deliverable) — due 2027-04-20 (owner: marissa_cole, michael_grant).
- Acme: share any additional compliance contacts & finalize network IPs — due 2027-04-19 (owner: Sarah Jenkins).
- Schedule kickoff: propose Wed 2027-04-21 14:00 PT — Marissa to send calendar invite once you confirm.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD-ACME-POC
